new_candidates.body:
## Summary

With stock genesis-world 1.4.6 + quadrants 1.4.0 on an AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950, `gs.gpu` -> AMDGPU backend), throughput in the stock speed benchmarks drops at large `n_envs`. Two of the three scenes we measured are slower at their largest N than at a smaller one:

- anymal_c at 65536 envs is about **3x slower** than at 16384.
- go2 at 131072 envs is about **2x slower** than at 16384.

The same shape is present on 1.4.5 + quadrants 1.3.3, so this is not a 1.4.6 regression.

## Numbers

Units: M env-steps/s. Each value is the median of 3 timed windows of 300 `scene.step()` calls, with a device sync around each window, after 200 warm-up steps. Each scene ran on one card, with the same card for all N of a scene. The table shows the median of 2 rounds.

| scene | N 4096 | N 8192 | N 16384 | large N |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `examples/speed_benchmark/anymal_c.py` | 5.26 | 6.46 | 8.28 | **2.73** (65536) |
| `examples/speed_benchmark/franka.py` | 6.82 | 9.74 | 15.52 | 17.09 (65536, flat) |
| `examples/locomotion` Go2Env (go2_train.py cfgs, random actions) | 1.24 | 1.94 | 2.94 | **1.34** (131072) |

For comparison, genesis-world 1.4.5 + quadrants 1.3.3 on the same cards:

| scene | N 16384 | large N |
|---|---|---|
| anymal_c | 6.06 | 3.43 (65536) |
| go2 | 2.98 | 1.74 (131072) |

A separate Go2 velocity-tracking task with PD gains and solver iterations pinned shows the same drop. Physics-only throughput is 3.78M at 16384 envs and 1.29M at 65536.

## What we checked

- **Collision / constraint buffer sizes.** Six buffer configurations at 65536 envs (including `max_collision_pairs` and the constraint buffer sizes) all gave about 1.11M env-steps/s on the Go2 task. Buffer sizing does not cause the drop.
- **Toolchain.** A plain source build of quadrants v1.4.0 behaves the same as the PyPI wheel (within 0.96-1.01x at every point).
- **Where the cost sits.** Experimental changes confined to the AMDGPU code generation in Quadrants (atomic memory ordering and launch-bound / block-size hints) raise anymal_c at 65536 from 2.73M to 19.1M and go2 at 131072 from 1.34M to 9.1M, with trajectories bitwise identical to stock on anymal_c and franka (go2 within stock run-to-run noise). This suggests the drop is in Quadrants' AMDGPU code generation or launch configuration rather than in Genesis' solver logic, but we have not isolated a single kernel.

## Repro

```bash
pip install genesis-world==1.4.6   # pulls quadrants 1.4.0
# examples/speed_benchmark/anymal_c.py at tag v1.4.6: change only the n_envs literal (16384 vs 65536)
python examples/speed_benchmark/anymal_c.py
```

Time `scene.step()` after warm-up, with a device sync around the timed window.

## Environment

- AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950), Linux
- Python 3.12, torch 2.11 (ROCm build)
- genesis-world 1.4.6, quadrants 1.4.0 (also 1.4.5 / 1.3.3)
- `gs.init(backend=gs.gpu, performance_mode=True)`, precision 32

We haven't tested whether the same happens on other GPU backends at these sizes. If useful, we can run a rocprof breakdown of the 16384 vs 65536 points.
new_candidates.title: AMDGPU: speed benchmarks get slower at large n_envs (anymal_c 65536 ~3x slower than 16384) on 1.4.6 / quadrants 1.4.0

new_candidates.body:
### Description
While reviewing Doxygen warnings and system docstrings:
1. In `tutorials/using_components.md`, the heading `## Related Resources` generates an anchor ID `resources`, which collides with `\page resources` in `tutorials/resources.md`, emitting:
   `warning: multiple use of section label 'resources'`
2. In `tutorials/component_jointforcecmd.md` and `tutorials/component_pose.md`, the syntax `extract a \ref gz::sim::Model "Model":` has a colon directly contacting the quote, which causes Doxygen to fail resolving the identifier and emit:
   `warning: unable to resolve reference to 'gz::sim::Model:' for \ref command`
3. In `src/systems/environmental_sensor_system/EnvironmentalSensorSystem.hh`, the `Tags:` block lacks standard Markdown list formatting, resulting in unsupported HTML/XML warnings for the parameter tags.
4. In `src/systems/touch_plugin/TouchPlugin.hh`, there is a grammatical typo (`a contact sensors is placed` instead of `a contact sensor is placed`) and missing backtick markup for the scoped collision name pattern.

### Expected Behavior
- Section labels should be unique across tutorials without collisions.
- `\ref` commands should resolve cleanly to the intended class.
- Parameter documentation should follow standard Markdown list conventions.

### Proposed Solution
- Rename heading in `using_components.md` to `## Additional References`.
- Add space before colon in the `\ref` targets in `component_jointforcecmd.md` and `component_pose.md`.
- Standardize `## System Parameters` markdown list in `EnvironmentalSensorSystem.hh`.
- Correct typo and markup in `TouchPlugin.hh`.
new_candidates.title: Documentation: Resolve Doxygen section label collision, ref parsing, and parameter warnings

new_candidates.body:
### Proposal

Add an opt-in `SO101_STS3215_CFG` next to `SO101_HIGH_PD_CFG`: the existing `DCMotorCfg` on the five arm joints with
per-joint values for the STS3215 servos under LeRobot's default registers (P 16, Acceleration 254, 12 V). Only
parameter values for stock Isaac Lab classes; `SO101_CFG` and the gripper stay as they are.

### Motivation

We replayed logged goals from 6 real SO-101 arms open loop (real start pose, tip error while moving, same metric for
every model):

| data | `SO101_CFG` (physx variant) | proposed `DCMotorCfg` |
|---|---|---|
| arm 1, 3 held-out loaded logs | 18.1 mm | **8.2 mm** |
| arm 2, [akoniti/dlsj-canonical](https://huggingface.co/datasets/akoniti/dlsj-canonical), 45 episodes | 15.0 mm | **6.1 mm** |
| 4 public LeRobot SO-101 datasets, 40 episodes | 22.5 mm | **14.5 mm** (better on all 4 arms) |
| lag behind the goal stream (real: 110 ms arm 2, 137 ms public) | 72 / 55 ms | **111 / 119 ms** |

The real follower runs 110-140 ms behind its targets; with these values the simulated arm does too, which matters for
policies that move between sim and the real arm.

Values (per joint: shoulder_pan, shoulder_lift, elbow_flex, wrist_flex, wrist_roll):

| | pan | lift | elbow | wrist_flex | wrist_roll |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| stiffness [N m/rad] | 18.20 | 20.79 | 20.56 | 20.23 | 12.31 |
| damping [N m s/rad] | 1.651 | 1.874 | 1.846 | 1.843 | 1.129 |
| saturation_effort [N m] | 7.152 | 6.891 | 7.138 | 7.152 | 7.152 |
| armature [kg m^2] | 0.0487 | 0.05775 | 0.05319 | 0.05468 | 0.0351 |
| friction = dynamic_friction [N m] | 0.1569 | 0.2969 | 0.2809 | 0.2056 | 0.105 |

`actuator_velocity_limit = saturation_effort / damping`, so the DC motor curve gives the servo's law
`clip(kp e, -sat, sat) - kd v` (duty limit on the P term, back-EMF outside it).

### Alternatives

`DelayedPDActuatorCfg` with a 16-20 ms delay scores the same (8.4 / 6.1 / 14.5 mm); the DC motor needs no delay
buffer. The 4 public datasets: lerobot/svla_so101_pickplace, ewinchell07/so101-spinning-table-all,
dongyoonkim/so101-eraser-90ep-wrist, DecisionFacts/Physical_AI_SO101_Test_Tube_Nesting_Task.

### Build Info

- Isaac Lab Version: 2.3.2 actuator classes (the `DCMotor` law is unchanged on main)
- Isaac Sim Version: 5.1.0 (PhysX, GPU, dt 0.5 ms)

### Additional context

Limit: one servo's values on all arms (registers on the public arms not logged, assumed LeRobot defaults); run on
Isaac Sim 5.1 PhysX, not yet on Isaac Lab 3.0 / Newton.

MuJoCo counterpart (same servos, same data): google-deepmind/mujoco_menagerie#368.

### Checklist

- [x] I have checked that there is no similar issue in the repo (**required**)

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `SO101_STS3215_CFG` in `so101.py` with a changelog fragment; `SO101_CFG` unchanged
- [ ] Loads and steps on PhysX and Newton

Happy to open the PR if this is welcome.
new_candidates.title: [Proposal] SO-101: DC motor actuator values that track real arms 1.5-2.4x closer than SO101_CFG

new_candidates.body:
The **ConcatenatePaths BT node** directly appends the poses of input_path2 to input_path1 without explicitly validating coordinate-frame compatibility or transforming poses into a common frame.

However, nav_msgs::msg::Path contains:
A message-level header defining the path's reference frame.
Individual PoseStamped headers associated with each pose.

In my case, I used
First mile: ComputePathToPose + ComputeRoute
Last mile: ComputeRoute + ComputePathToPose

But, if the input paths originate from different coordinate frames (e.g., map and odom), directly appending their poses could produce an invalid path. **The current BT's implementation  preserves the header of input_path1 (falling back to input_path2 if necessary), but does not modify the individual PoseStamped headers of the appended poses.**

Consequently, if the two input paths use different coordinate frames, the resulting Path could contain poses expressed in different frames while having only one path-level header.

Questions:
- Should ConcatenatePaths validate that both input paths use compatible frames?
- Should the node transform poses into a common frame when the input frames differ?
- Should individual pose headers also be validated against the resulting Path header?

Expected Behaviour:
The node should either enforce a common-frame contract or transform the input poses into a common coordinate frame before concatenation. This would prevent potentially invalid paths from being passed to downstream navigation components.
new_candidates.title: Potential Coordinate Frame Inconsistency in ConcatenatedPaths

new_candidates.body:
The collision test suite has no ConvexMesh contact check near the contact-distance threshold, so a broadphase AABB that is too small would go unnoticed.

The convex cases in `collision_sphere_sphere_unit` and `collision_box_box_unit` (built with `makeConvexMesh`) expect contacts 20–150 mm inside the contact distance (e.g. distance 0.5 at margin 0.52, 0.1 at margin 0.25). A ConvexMesh AABB 10 mm too small per side would drop real contacts and still pass all of them.

Until now the Bullet hull AABB carried 40 mm of slack per side (the stale `CONVEX_DISTANCE_MARGIN`), which hid this. #1413 makes it exact, which is correct but leaves no slack between the AABB and the contact distance. The broadphase is then only right if the AABB is never too small, and nothing tests that.

Proposed test: two ConvexMesh unit cubes face to face, at contact distances 10, 30 and 100 mm, along each axis. Expect one contact at the exact distance 0.1 mm inside the threshold and none 0.1 mm outside, for the Bullet simple, Bullet BVH and FCL discrete managers.
new_candidates.title: Collision test suite has no ConvexMesh contact check near the contact-distance threshold
